summary.headline: Sutlej Textiles Q2 FY27 standalone income Rs 830 crore (vs Rs 642 crore) and PAT Rs 6.7 crore vs loss of Rs 14 crore a year ago.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 standalone income of Rs 830 crore against Rs 642 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA of Rs 53.4 crore (6.4% margin) versus Rs 17 crore in Q2 FY26. H1 FY27 EBITDA was Rs 101 crore at a 6.5% margin, and profit after tax turned positive at Rs 6.7 crore in Q2 and Rs 9.5 crore in H1 against losses a year earlier. Management attributed the improvement to product portfolio rationalisation, efficiency gains and a shift toward value-added products, and said all three business verticals are now EBITDA positive. Working capital rose on higher material prices and inventory, and debt-equity is about 1.1x. Q&A was dominated by analyst probing on why historical margins lagged peers, which management answered only partly, deferring detail to offline discussions.

segments.name: Yarn (spinning)
segments.commentary: Management said yarn EBITDA margins were flat QoQ despite a sharp rise in freight costs; the company says the value-added product direction should support better margins in coming quarters. Yarn remains the core business, with about 15,500 employees and headcount falling deliberately.

segments.name: Home textiles
segments.commentary: Volume (meterage) grew about 30% YoY, with mix shift driving value growth. Gross block is Rs 110 crore; management targets about Rs 250 crore turnover this year, and order book visibility is about five months.

segments.name: Technical textiles
segments.commentary: Qualification is approved and equipment is being installed, expected to be settled by end of Q4 FY27, with commercial contribution from FY28.

guidance_outlook: Management expects margin direction to give better fractions in coming quarters, but gave no numeric margin guidance.
Home textiles turnover target of about Rs 250 crore this year; intent to double the business over two years, without rushing.
Technical textiles contribution expected to begin from FY28, with supply from outside India.
Power cost reduced to about 9.9% from about 12-12.5% last year; management targets a 1.5 percentage point manpower cost gap versus peers through modernisation.
Capital allocation to shift toward downstream, value-added businesses; modernisation of fibre dyeing and yarn units is phased and capex-dependent.
capex_capacity: Gross block in home textiles is Rs 110 crore; expansion underway in weaving and yarn-dyeing capacity, with processing capacity partly already in place.
Modernisation of the fibre dyeing unit in the yarn business is in a phased approach, with spindle replacement planned.
Company operates about 400,000+ spindles; management said some spindles are outdated and part of the fleet may be scrapped as part of a portfolio rebalancing.
Technical textiles equipment is on the way and expected to be settled by end of Q4 FY27.
Capital allocation to be funded through internal accruals and existing financing arrangements.
demand_pricing: Home textiles: about 30% meterage growth YoY; order book covers about five months; price increase was small and growth was mainly from product mix.
Yarn: freight costs rose sharply in Q2, and raw material prices lagged pass-through to customers, limiting margins.
Management says it earns margins on export products even with freight costs up, citing about $2,000-2,500 per container versus $10,000 earlier.
New export push into Africa and Middle East for finished fabrics using own yarn and external weaving partners; also a PV fabric export segment started.
Working capital increased on higher material prices and inventory, but management says it remains within its envisaged range.

qa_highlights.question: Why are emitter (yarn) margins flat QoQ, and do you expect better margins in the next six months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yarn margins held flat despite a sharp freight cost increase and raw material pass-through lag; it expects the portfolio direction to give better margins in coming quarters, without a number.

qa_highlights.question: What is home textile volume growth and the capital needed to double turnover?
qa_highlights.answer: Meterage grew about 30% YoY with mix-led value growth; gross block is Rs 110 crore and the Rs 250 crore turnover target is for this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why have historical EBITDA margins lagged the industry, and is the equipment outdated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a shift in the segment, slow machine upgrades, higher employee cost and higher power cost (about 12-12.5% of costs, now 9.9%). It said some spindles are outdated and that it is rebalancing the portfolio, but did not give a full answer and offered an offline discussion.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the margin improvement, and what is the home textile order pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the margins are sustainable given the current freight environment, and home textile orders are booked for about five months, with the doubling target pursued without rushing.

qa_highlights.question: Status of technical textiles customer approvals and FY28 timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Qualification is complete; equipment should be settled by end of Q4 FY27 and commercial supply from FY28 is on track.

risks_watch: Sustainability of margin gains: yarn margins flat QoQ and freight and raw material costs remain volatile.
Capex needs for modernisation and spindle replacement versus a balance sheet at about 1.1x debt-equity and rising working capital.
Management did not fully explain the long-running gap versus peer margins; the equipment-versus-operations question remains open.
Technical textiles ramp-up depends on equipment installation by end Q4 FY27 and FY28 commercial start.
Home textiles doubling target and the Rs 250 crore turnover goal need to be tracked against the order book.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic and somewhat defensive: management stressed the structural turnaround and profit recovery, but was vague on the root cause of historical underperformance and deferred detailed questions to offline meetings.
key_quotes: Importantly, the improvement is increasingly broad-based with all the three business verticals continue to remain EBITDA positive.
Looking ahead, we remain cautiously optimistic about the business.
We are fixing one thing at a time, right?

growth.why: Home textiles FY27 turnover target of about Rs 250 crore (vs gross block Rs 110 crore) is backed by about five months of order book and weaving/yarn-dyeing expansion underway, but no timing or numeric capacity for that expansion was given; yarn margin guidance is directional only and technical textiles contributes only from FY28.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 6.4% vs about 2% a year ago (Rs 53.4 cr vs Rs 17 cr), power cost cut to ~9.9% from 12-12.5%, and management expects better margin direction, though yarn margins were flat QoQ and no numeric guide was given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Home textiles weaving and yarn-dyeing expansion is under construction against a Rs 110 cr gross block, and technical textiles equipment is due to be settled by end Q4 FY27, though no numeric capacity or timing was given for the home textiles build.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Home textiles meterage grew about 30% YoY with about five months of order book, and export push into Africa and Middle East is starting, though yarn volumes are not guided.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management is upgrading plant and machinery and running a phased fibre-dyeing modernisation and spindle replacement from a 400,000+ spindle base, with capex funded from internal accruals; utilisation was not disclosed, so the size and timing of the next board-level announcement is unclear.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Home textiles turnover target of about Rs 250 cr this year is new and management says it will achieve it, but there is no numeric margin or revenue guide to upgrade and yarn margins were flat QoQ.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Freight costs rose sharply in Q2, raw material pass-through lags, working capital rose on higher inventory, and debt-equity is about 1.1x, so yarn margins could be squeezed if these persist.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Technical textiles qualification is approved with commercial contribution from FY28 and a PV fabric export segment has already started, though no product count or revenue was quantified.

rows.label: Profitability turnaround: PAT positive
rows.why: PAT was Rs 6.7 cr in Q2 FY27 vs loss of Rs 14 cr a year ago, and H1 PAT Rs 9.5 cr vs loss of Rs 44.1 cr, with all three verticals now EBITDA positive.

rows.label: Export push into Africa and Middle East
rows.why: Finished fabric exports using own yarn and external weaving partners are starting, with freight at about $2,000-2,500 per container vs $10,000 earlier, though no export revenue was quantified.

rows.label: Working capital build
rows.why: Working capital rose on higher material prices and inventory, and debt-equity is about 1.1x, so cash conversion could stay weak even as the company says it is within its envisaged range.

tone.note: Management was confident on the profit turnaround, power cost cut and home textiles growth, but cautious on yarn margins and vague on why historical margins lagged peers, deferring detail offline; analysts pressed on the peer margin gap and outdated equipment.
